alignments.note: Aorist imperative rendered by the bare English imperative.
Quantifier on its own word. Rule 80 does not apply: the ASV writes a separate word for the article as well, so the ordinary split holds.
Substantival article before a participle: rule 32 gives it the pronoun *them* and nothing else, the participle keeping the relative clause.

Participle rendered as a finite relative clause; *that* and *have* are rule 7 and 9 helpers on it. Rule 17 heads the support-verb rendering *have the rule* on the meaning-bearing complement *rule* rather than on the auxiliary-like *have*.

Genitive complement of the participle: *over* realizes the bare case and rides with the pronoun, no Greek preposition being expressed and no article standing to anchor it, exactly as at HEB.13.7, HEB.13.17 and HEB.13.24 alike. 2CO.11.2 `ὑμᾶς` → *over you* reads a bare case the same way unhedged, and 2CO.1.24 is the same support-verb shape — `κυριεύομεν` → *we have lordship* with `πίστεως` → *over faith* — though hedged and conceding the other reading. That other reading is live and the corpus does not settle it: 1PE.5.3 `κατακυριεύοντες` → *lording it over* keeps *over* inside the verb's unit unhedged, and the corpus generally keeps a bare-case particle on an English phrasal verb, as `ἀνέχομαι` → *bear with* does in four units and as this chapter's own HEB.13.22 and HEB.13.14 *we seek after* do. I take the complement here because `ἡγέομαι` has no corpus unit of its own to follow and the nearest same-shape precedent is 2CO.1.24's *have + noun + over*, where the English preposition heads a phrase expressing the people ruled rather than being a particle the verb selects; reading it as the idiom's own particle remains defensible.
Second quantifier on its own word.
Substantival adjective rendered by the noun *saints*; the article beside it has already taken the determiner under rule 58.
Present indicative rendered by the bare verb; the subject is the articular phrase at s012.

Substantival article with a prepositional modifier and no participle: rule 22's case. The ASV supplies no relativizer and no copula here, so unlike `οἱ μετ' αὐτοῦ` → *they … that are with him* the article takes only *They*.
Preposition realized by *of*. It is not left `unrepresented` under rule 36, since an English preposition is written for it.
Article before a name with no English determiner: rule 23. Rule 21 forbids leaving a bare *of* on it, so the preposition stays on s013.

review_notes: s003/s004 split follows rule 32 (`οἱ κατοικοῦντες` → *they* / *that dwell*); the competing reading would give *them that* whole to the article, which rule 32 refuses.
s004 head: *rule* rather than *have*, per rule 17's support-verb clause (`bear witness` heads on *witness*).
s005: *over* assigned to the genitive pronoun rather than read as part of a phrasal *have the rule over*, per rule 36.

s012: the packet's alternative rendering note (*The brethren from Italy*) would supply a noun for the article; the ASV's own *They of Italy* is what is aligned here, and rule 12 bars a new textual decision in the alignment file.
All 15 source and 18 target ids partitioned exactly once.
